summary: The vDSO reads fine time from the TSC when available and coarse time from the data page in every mode; each case boots the test image on two processors and runs vdsomusl

cases.behavior: Under rach2.tscreliable, on two processors, the x86-64 vDSO is mapped where AT_SYSINFO_EHDR says, its functions are found as libc finds them, and the clock calls it answers read the TSC and agree with the system call's, in order on every processor, and make no system call by the kernel's count

assertions.checks: on the i686 kernel an image has no AT_SYSINFO_EHDR, and maps names neither [vvar] nor [vdso]
AT_SYSINFO_EHDR gives the ELF header of a shared object of the program's class and machine, x86-64's or for an i686 program i386's
/proc/self/maps has [vvar], two r--p pages, just below AT_SYSINFO_EHDR and [vdso], one r-xp page, at it

the image's hash and version tables give __vdso_clock_gettime, __vdso_gettimeofday, __vdso_time, __vdso_getcpu and __vdso_clock_getres of version LINUX_2.6, and the 32-bit image also __vdso_clock_gettime64 of LINUX_2.6 and __kernel_vsyscall, __kernel_sigreturn and __kernel_rt_sigreturn of LINUX_2.5
/proc/stat's vdso_tsc is 1
real time, the monotonic, raw and boot clocks and the two coarse clocks read through the vDSO, and its gettimeofday and time, each lie between two readings by the system call
the vDSO's clock_getres gives what the system call gives for clocks 0 to 7, and its clock_gettime and clock_getres give -EINVAL for clock 12
pinned to each processor in turn, the vDSO's getcpu and sched_getcpu give that processor, on node 0
a million monotonic readings through the vDSO on one processor, and two thousand on each processor in turn, never go back

a child's mprotect makes [vdso] rwxp, a store there does not fault and its clock_gettime works, another child's write through /proc/self/mem reads back with the page still r-xp, and the parent's vDSO is unchanged, as Linux copies the page on a write

a read of [vvar] through /proc/self/mem and a tracer's PTRACE_PEEKDATA of a tracee's [vvar] give EIO, process_vm_readv of it and a vmsplice of a byte of it into a pipe EFAULT, and mprotect of it with PROT_EXEC EACCES, as on Linux, whose get_user_pages refuses the region
40,000 fine readings and 60,000 coarse readings, including direct calls of __vdso_time, each raise /proc/stat's clock_calls by fewer than 1,000 per group

native.reason: the processor must report no invariant TSC, as QEMU's max model does, where the Lenovo's reports one, which guest.vdso.tsc's native run covers

cases.behavior: Under rach2.notsc the x86-64 kernel's vDSOs make system calls for fine clock readings and read time and the coarse clocks from the data page. The i686 kernel maps no vDSO, so every clock reading makes a system call

of 40,000 fine and 60,000 coarse readings, clock_calls counts the fine group on the x86-64 kernel and both groups on i686, allowing fewer than 1,000 extra calls per group. The coarse group reads both coarse clocks and calls __vdso_time directly where mapped

native.reason: this case needs a boot with rach2.notsc to disable the vDSO's fine clock

ia32.why: the i686 kernel maps no vDSO, while the x86-64 kernel gives an i386 program the 32-bit vDSO, as Linux's does; vdsomusl reports the group kernel from ETUDE_KERNEL, the kernel's architecture, and checks the 32-bit image's own functions there
